DEFINITION · qeva:1:hierarchy@1

Hierarchy and scale

A hierarchy organizes objects or descriptions across ordered or nested levels with explicit relations between levels.

editorialsystems · order · information
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

A hierarchical description says what belongs above, below, inside, or at a coarser scale—and how levels connect.

EXACT

The compact statement

One formal model is a partially ordered set (L,≤) of levels together with state spaces X_l and maps C_{l→m}:X_l→X_m for selected l≤m.

Example

Pixels → blocks → regions is a simple multiscale hierarchy when each coarser level aggregates the finer one.

Boundary / caveat

Hierarchy is a broad structural pattern, not one unique mathematical object. Claims of “emergent invariance across levels” require a specified cross-level map and invariant.

Assumptions

  • A family of levels and relations or maps between levels are specified.
